newsitem.title: USA: Lands' End 8-week holiday sales up.
newsitem.headline: Lands' End 8-week holiday sales up.

text.p: Lands' End Inc said Thursday that its net sales for the eight weeks ended December 27 totaled $334 million, up six percent from $315 million during the nine-week period ended December 29, 1995.
Net income for the eight-week period was $33.6 million or $1.03 a share, up from $25.3 million or $0.75 a year for the nine-week holiday period in 1995, it added.
Earnings from the year-ago nine-week period included an after-tax charge of $1.1 million or $0.03 a share.
Adjusting the calendar for a comparable number of weeks, net sales for the holiday period were up 14 percent.

Inventory as of December 27, 1996, was $130 million, down from $164 million on December 29, 1995. Liquidation of excess inventory totaled about five percent of net sales during the eight-week 1996 period, compared with six percent a year ago.

Lands' End said it began the holiday period with lower inventory because of strong sales in the third quarter. Lower inventory in the holiday period resulted in higher levels of lost sales and back orders, which hurt overall sales.
Gross profit in the eight-week period was $157.9 million, or 47.2 percent of net sales, up from $139.0 million or 44.1 percent of net sales in the prior year's nine-week period.

For the 47-week period ended December 27, 1996, net sales were $1.03 billion, up nine percent from $947.0 million in the 48-week period a year ago. Net income in the first 47 weeks of fiscal 1997 was $47.1 million or $1.42 a share, up from $30.0 million or $0.88 a share a year ago.
Lands' End fiscal year will end on January 31, 1997. Year-end results are expected to be reported in mid-March.
